pests.symptoms: Fine webbing, browning needles, common in dry heated air.
pests.treatment: Raise humidity, rinse foliage, apply insecticidal soap.

issues.symptom: Lower branches turning brown and dropping
issues.cause: Low humidity, insufficient light, or being too close to a heating vent
issues.fix: Raise humidity, move to brighter indirect light, and keep away from heat sources — note that dropped lower branches don't regrow.
Let soil dry slightly more between waterings.
Rotate the pot a quarter turn every couple of weeks.

light: Bright indirect light; some gentle direct morning sun.
water: No soil — soak in room-temperature water for 20-30 minutes once or twice a week, then shake off excess water and let fully dry within 4 hours (upside down) to prevent rot.
soil: None; grows without soil (epiphyte). Needs good airflow.
humidity: Prefers moderate to high humidity between soakings.
fertilizer: Diluted bromeliad/air plant fertilizer monthly, mixed into the soak water.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.symptoms: White cottony clusters at the base.
pests.treatment: Remove with alcohol swab; rinse well afterward.

issues.symptom: Leaves turning brown, dry, and crispy — often at the base first
issues.cause: Underwatering or air that's too dry
issues.fix: Soak more frequently (2-3 times a week) and mist between soaks.

issues.symptom: Base turns dark, mushy, and leaves pull out easily
issues.cause: Rot from not drying out fully after soaking, or water pooling in the base
issues.fix: Always shake off excess water and dry upside down; never let the plant sit wet, especially in the crown.
Increase soaking frequency.

light: Bright light including some direct sun.
water: Let soil dry out between waterings; drought tolerant succulent.
fertilizer: Diluted balanced fertilizer monthly during growing season, none while blooming.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.symptoms: White cottony clusters on stems.
pests.treatment: Remove with alcohol swab, treat with insecticidal soap.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.symptoms: Clusters on flower buds and new growth.
pests.treatment: Rinse off and apply insecticidal soap.

issues.fix: Let soil dry out fully, trim rot, repot in dry succulent mix.

issues.symptom: No reblooming after the first flush of flowers
issues.cause: Kalanchoe needs long uninterrupted dark periods (like poinsettias) to rebloom
issues.fix: Give it 14 hours of complete darkness nightly for several weeks to trigger new buds, or treat as an annual bloom.
Move to a brighter, sunnier spot.

light: Bright indirect light; no direct sun.
water: Let the top inch of soil dry out between waterings; avoid wetting the leaves.
fertilizer: Diluted balanced fertilizer monthly in growing season.

pests.name: Powdery mildew (fungal, not a pest)
pests.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves, common in poor air circulation.
pests.treatment: Improve airflow, avoid wetting foliage, and treat with a fungicide labeled for powdery mildew if it spreads.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.symptoms: White cottony clusters.
pests.treatment: Remove with alcohol swab, treat with insecticidal soap.

issues.cause: Powdery mildew fungus, usually from poor airflow or high humidity with stagnant air
issues.fix: Improve air circulation, avoid overhead watering, remove badly affected leaves, apply fungicide if needed.
Raise humidity and avoid placing near heating/cooling vents.
Let soil dry more between waterings.

light: Bright indirect light to some direct sun for best color.
water: Keep soil consistently moist; doesn't tolerate drying out well.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer every 2-4 weeks in growing season.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.symptoms: Small insects clustered on new growth and stems.
pests.treatment: Rinse off with water and apply insecticidal soap.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.symptoms: White cottony clusters at leaf joints.
pests.treatment: Remove with alcohol swab, treat with insecticidal soap.

issues.symptom: Wilting even though soil feels moist
issues.cause: Root rot from overwatering, or heat stress
issues.fix: Check roots for rot if soil is soggy; move out of intense heat and improve drainage.

issues.cause: Insufficient light or not being pinched back
issues.fix: Move to brighter light and regularly pinch growing tips to encourage bushiness.
Move to a brighter spot with some direct sun.
Water more frequently — coleus dries out quickly and doesn't like to stay dry.

light: Bright indirect light; tolerates medium light.
water: Let the top 1-2 in of soil dry out between waterings; semi-succulent, sensitive to overwatering.
humidity: Tolerates average humidity, prefers slightly more.
fertilizer: Diluted balanced fertilizer monthly in growing season.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.symptoms: White cottony clusters at leaf/stem joints.
pests.treatment: Remove with alcohol swab, treat with insecticidal soap.

issues.symptom: Soft, mushy, translucent leaves and stems
issues.cause: Overwatering / rot (very common with this semi-succulent plant)
issues.fix: Let soil dry out fully, trim mushy stems, repot in fast-draining mix, water less often.
Water thoroughly and resume regular watering.

issues.symptom: Long thin stems with small leaves
issues.fix: Move to brighter indirect light.

light: Bright indirect light with some direct sun for blooming.
water: Let soil dry out most of the way between waterings; semi-succulent vine, sensitive to overwatering.
soil: Well-draining, chunky potting mix with perlite/bark.
fertilizer: Diluted balanced fertilizer monthly in growing season.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.symptoms: White cottony clusters at leaf/stem joints.
pests.treatment: Remove with alcohol swab, treat with insecticidal soap.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.symptoms: Clusters on flower buds and new growth, sticky residue.
pests.treatment: Rinse off and apply insecticidal soap.

issues.symptom: Soft, wrinkled or yellowing leaves with wet soil
issues.fix: Let soil dry out more thoroughly between waterings and ensure fast drainage.
Water thoroughly and resume regular sparse watering.

issues.cause: Insufficient light, or flower spurs were pruned off
issues.fix: Move to brighter light with some direct sun, and never trim off the short spurs flowers regrow from.

light: Bright indirect light; no direct sun.
water: Keep the central 'cup' rosette filled with fresh water (flush and refill every 1-2 weeks), and keep soil lightly moist.
fertilizer: Very diluted balanced fertilizer occasionally; bromeliads need little feeding.

pests.name: Scale
pests.symptoms: Small brown bumps on leaves.
pests.treatment: Scrape off and treat with horticultural oil.

issues.fix: Empty and refill the cup with fresh water every 1-2 weeks.

issues.symptom: Mother plant fading and dying after flowering
issues.cause: Normal life cycle — bromeliads bloom once then decline, producing offset 'pups'
issues.fix: This is normal; let pups grow to about a third the size of the parent before separating and potting them.
Raise humidity and use filtered water in the cup.

light: Low to medium indirect light; extremely tolerant of neglect and shade.
water: Let soil dry out between waterings; very forgiving.
fertilizer: Light feeding with balanced fertilizer 1-2 times in summer.

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.symptoms: Rare; fine webbing in very dry conditions.
pests.treatment: Wipe leaves and apply insecticidal soap if seen.

issues.cause: Overwatering (uncommon since it's very tolerant, but possible)
issues.fix: Let soil dry out more between waterings.

issues.cause: Direct sun exposure or extended drought
issues.fix: Move out of direct sun and water more regularly.

issues.cause: Normal — this plant is naturally slow-growing regardless of care
issues.fix: No action needed; be patient.

light: Bright indirect light; tolerates medium light.
water: Let the top 1-2 in of soil dry out between waterings.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid fertilizer monthly in growing season.

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.symptoms: Fine webbing and stippling on leaves.
pests.treatment: Wipe leaves and apply insecticidal soap.

pests.name: Scale
pests.symptoms: Brown bumps on stems, sticky leaves.
pests.treatment: Scrape off and treat with horticultural oil.

issues.symptom: Yellow leaves dropping with wet soil
issues.fix: Let soil dry more between waterings and check drainage.

light: Bright light, including several hours of direct sun.
water: Let soil dry out fully between waterings; very drought tolerant.
soil: Fast-draining potting mix, cactus/succulent blend works well.
fertilizer: Light feeding with balanced fertilizer a couple times in summer.

pests.name: Spider mites
pests.symptoms: Fine webbing, speckled leaves.
pests.treatment: Wipe leaves and apply insecticidal soap.

issues.cause: Underwatering, low humidity, or mineral buildup
issues.fix: Water thoroughly on a regular schedule and flush soil occasionally.
Move to a sunnier location.

light: Bright, indirect light; no direct sun, which scorches leaves.
water: If grown in water, change it weekly and keep roots fully submerged; if in soil, keep evenly moist. Very sensitive to fluoride/chlorine.
soil: Often grown in water with pebbles, or well-draining soil.
fertilizer: A drop of diluted liquid fertilizer once a month if grown in water.

pests.name: Mealybugs
pests.symptoms: White cottony clusters on stems.
pests.treatment: Remove with alcohol swab, treat with insecticidal soap.

issues.cause: Tap water chemicals (chlorine/fluoride), direct sun, or old stagnant water
issues.fix: Use filtered or distilled water, change water weekly, and move out of direct sun.

issues.cause: Water not changed often enough, allowing bacterial growth
issues.fix: Change water weekly, trim off blackened roots, rinse the container thoroughly.

issues.cause: Tap water minerals or dry air
issues.fix: Switch to filtered/distilled water.

light: Very bright light, ideally several hours of direct sun daily (a sunny windowsill or grow light).
water: Keep soil constantly wet using only distilled, rain, or reverse-osmosis water in a tray (tap water minerals will kill it). Never let it dry out.
soil: Nutrient-free, acidic mix: unfertilized sphagnum peat moss mixed with perlite or sand — never regular potting soil or fertilizer.
temperature: 70-80°F (21-27°C) in summer; needs a cooler winter dormancy period around 35-50°F (2-10°C).
fertilizer: None in soil — never fertilize the soil. It gets nutrients from catching insects; do not feed it hamburger meat or human food.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.symptoms: Small insects on new growth/flower stalks.
pests.treatment: Rinse off gently with distilled water; avoid chemical pesticides which can harm the plant.

issues.cause: Normal — individual traps naturally die after a few catches/openings, or from tap water minerals
issues.fix: Trim off blackened traps; ensure only distilled/rain water is used going forward.

issues.symptom: No traps closing or weak response
issues.cause: Insufficient light or the plant is stressed/exhausted from too much manual triggering
issues.fix: Increase direct light exposure and avoid triggering traps without feeding them.

issues.symptom: Plant turning entirely black and mushy
issues.cause: Tap water minerals/fertilizer poisoning, or rot from poor dormancy conditions
issues.fix: Switch immediately to distilled/rain water only, use nutrient-free soil, and provide a proper cool winter dormancy.
Move to the sunniest spot available or supplement with a strong grow light.
